name: reversal-hysteresis-multiplier
rationale: The 2026-09-11 report's post-mortem on the rejected min-notional-aware-rebalance ended with an explicit recommendation that has never been tested: 'add hysteresis/cooldown so a lot-sized overshoot cannot trigger its own reversal'. Its evidence was a near-symmetric 3,744 buys against 4,751 sells — a ping-pong in which each correction manufactured the opposite delta. The 2026-09-12 baseline shows the same signature without any rounding involved: at 500,000 JPY, 754 trades in 14 days at an 11.7% win rate, i.e. seven trades in eight lose, which is what a position oscillating across a single threshold looks like rather than a strategy taking directional views. The current gate is sign-agnostic — it tests |delta| >= allocation_threshold whether the delta continues the last trade or reverses it — so reversing costs exactly as little as continuing. This hypothesis makes reversals strictly more expensive to trigger than continuations: after a fill, an opposite-signed delta must clear allocation_threshold * reversal_threshold_multiplier, while a same-signed delta clears the unchanged threshold. It is deliberately asymmetric, because the failure mode being targeted is asymmetric — letting a winning direction keep running while damping the oscillation is the whole point, and a symmetric cooldown (the other reading of the 2026-09-11 note) would suppress both equally.
code_change_summary: Add one new field to TradingConfig (src/config.rs): `reversal_threshold_multiplier: f64`, with `#[serde(default = "default_reversal_threshold_multiplier")]` returning 1.0 so every existing stored config and every existing hypothesis file deserialises to exactly today's behaviour (1.0 makes the reversal gate identical to the normal gate, i.e. a no-op). Add it to TradingConfig::default() as 1.0, and extend TradingConfig::validate() to require it to be >= 1.0 and finite, with a Japanese error message matching the style of the existing messages. Confirm the DB round-trip in src/storage/config.rs still works (the repository serialises the whole struct as JSON, so a serde default is sufficient — verify this rather than assuming, and extend the config round-trip test to cover the new field). Then apply the gate. Track the side of the last EXECUTED fill: add a field to TradingEngine (src/trading/engine.rs) such as `last_fill_side: Option<OrderSide>`, initialised None, set to the order's side immediately after RiskManager returns Allow and the order is actually sent, at both live call sites (around lines 485 and 562); and a matching local variable in Simulator::run (src/backtest/simulator.rs), set in the RiskDecision::Allow arm after exchange.send_order. Introduce one shared pub(crate) associated function on TradingEngine so the two paths cannot drift, e.g. `fn effective_threshold(delta: f64, last_fill_side: Option<OrderSide>, allocation_threshold: f64, reversal_threshold_multiplier: f64) -> f64`, returning `allocation_threshold * reversal_threshold_multiplier` when last_fill_side is Some and the delta's implied side (Buy for delta > 0.0, Sell for delta < 0.0) is the OPPOSITE of it, and plain `allocation_threshold` otherwise (including when last_fill_side is None, i.e. before the first fill). Document it with the rule and a NOTE citing this hypothesis and the 2026-09-11 ping-pong observation. At all three call sites, replace the bare `allocation_threshold` in the comparison with the value this function returns; leave everything downstream untouched. Do not change compute_btc_target, apply_zone, sticky_target, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic. In your report, state the resulting buy/sell split and total_trades alongside the baseline's, so the report can say whether the oscillation actually fell rather than only whether Sharpe moved. Add unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs's test module covering: no prior fill (multiplier inert, threshold unchanged); prior Buy with a positive delta (continuation, threshold unchanged); prior Buy with a negative delta whose magnitude is between threshold and threshold*multiplier (gated, no order); prior Buy with a negative delta above threshold*multiplier (allowed); the mirror cases for a prior Sell; and reversal_threshold_multiplier == 1.0 reproducing the pre-change threshold exactly in every case. Add a TradingConfig::validate() test rejecting a multiplier below 1.0.
constraints: This hypothesis does NOT need to modify the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target, and MUST NOT do so — the signal is held fixed so the measured effect is attributable to the gating change alone.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) or its body.

The new TradingConfig field MUST default to 1.0 and MUST be a strict no-op at that value, so that every config already persisted in a DB and every existing hypothesis file continues to produce byte-identical behaviour. Verify this by running the baseline config through the changed binary and confirming the report is identical to the pre-change baseline before running the variant.

MUST apply the change at ALL THREE call sites (both live sites in src/trading/engine.rs and the one in src/backtest/simulator.rs), so the backtest cannot measure a strategy the live engine would not run.

MUST key the gate on the side of an ACTUALLY EXECUTED fill (after RiskDecision::Allow and send_order), never on a merely intended or lot-floor-suppressed order — otherwise at the 50,000 JPY primary capital, where the baseline suppressed 5,960 rebalances below the lot size, the gate would be driven almost entirely by orders that never happened.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, the exchange lot-size check, the RiskManager gates, or the fee logic.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the existing config, compute_btc_target_* and simulator tests — update an expected value only where the new gate legitimately changes it (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically — a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff changes the order-triggering condition on the LIVE order-submission path and adds a persisted TradingConfig field, per the 'anything touching live trading behavior gets flagged explicitly' rule in docs/self-improvement-loop.md.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the bitFlyer REST/WS client.
